title: A novel medium for long-term primary culture of hemocytes of Metapenaeus ensis
author: Zhao, Guo
materials: For amino acids, as shown in Table 2, there are 5 kinds of stock solutions (A, B, C, D and E) with a concentration of 100× needed to prepare, based on the solubility of amino acids (water-, acid- and alkali-soluble) and their contents in the medium. Of them, stock solution A consists of 12 kinds of water-soluble amino acids of glycine, L‑serine, l-valine, l-lysine, l-alanine, β-alanine, ornithine, l-arginine, l-threonine, hydroxyproline, 4-hydroxybutanoic acid (γ-ABA) and l-glutamine. Stock solution B and C are water-soluble taurine and l-proline, respectively. Stock solution D includes 5 kinds of alkali-soluble amino acids of l-histidine, l-isoleucine, l-asparagine, l-methionine and l-phenylalanine, which are pre-dissolved in 1 M NaOH and then diluted in water. Stock solution E includes 7 kinds of acid-soluble amino acids of l-cystine, l-leucine, l-tyrosine, l-aspartic acid, l-glutamic acid, l-cysteine and l-tryptophan, which are pre-dissolved in 1 M HCl and then diluted in water.

For saccharides, there are 2 kinds of stock solutions F and G with a concentration of 100× needed to prepare. Stock solution F consists of 11 kinds of water-soluble saccharides (xylose, fucose, ribose, sucrose, lactose, fructose, arabinose, trehalose, gentiobiose, D+ Galactose and sodium pyruvate). Stock solution G contains only glucose which is water-soluble in water.

For vitamins, there are 2 kinds of stock solutions (H and I) with a concentration of 100× needed to prepare. Stock solution H is made up of 7 kinds of water-soluble vitamins including i-inositol, niacinamide, choline chloride, d-calcium pantothenate, thiamine monophosphate, pyridoxine hydrochloride and riboflavin 5′-phosphate Na. Stock solution I contains only folic acid which is alkali-soluble in 1 M NaOH.

For inorganic salts, there are also 2 kinds of stock solutions (J and K) needed to prepare. Stock solution J is a mixture of 3 kinds of water-soluble inorganic salts of MgSO4, KH2PO4, and Na2HPO4 with a concentration of 100×. Stock solution K is a mixture of 4 kinds of water-soluble inorganic salts of NaCl, KCl, MgCl2 and CaCl2 with a concentration of 25×. Instead of a stock solution, the pH regulator salt of NaHCO3 is added in powder separately just before used.
The stock solution L which contains phenol red only is prepared as a pH indicator to a concentration of 100×.
All the above-mentioned stock solutions are stored at −80 ℃ until used.

steps.title: Prepare amino acid stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make five 100× amino‑acid stock solutions (A–E) according to their solubility, using the concentrations listed in Table 2.

substeps.instruction: Stock A (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve glycine 15 484 mg L⁻¹, L‑serine 3 552 mg L⁻¹, L‑valine 1 808 mg L⁻¹, L‑lysine 15 360 mg L⁻¹, L‑alanine 1 848 mg L⁻¹, β‑alanine 433 mg L⁻¹, ornithine 1 656 mg L⁻¹, L‑arginine 25 558 mg L⁻¹, L‑threonine 1 305 mg L⁻¹, hydroxyproline 5 629 mg L⁻¹, γ‑ABA 283 mg L⁻¹, L‑glutamine 30 000 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water; adjust to 100× by volume.
Stock B (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve taurine 74.7 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.
Stock C (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve L‑proline 136.6 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.

Stock D (alkali‑soluble, 100×): dissolve L‑histidine 2 638 mg L⁻¹, L‑isoleucine 5 089 mg L⁻¹, L‑asparagine 14 701 mg L⁻¹, L‑methionine 703 mg L⁻¹, L‑phenylalanine 3 910 mg L⁻¹ in 1 M NaOH, then dilute with sterile water to 100×.

Stock E (acid‑soluble, 100×): dissolve L‑cystine 2 165 mg L⁻¹, L‑leucine 8 105 mg L⁻¹, L‑tyrosine 558 mg L⁻¹, L‑aspartic acid 4 851 mg L⁻¹, L‑glutamic acid 8 859 mg L⁻¹, L‑cysteine 12 000 mg L⁻¹, L‑tryptophan 2 000 mg L⁻¹ in 1 M HCl, then dilute with sterile water to 100×.

steps.title: Prepare saccharide stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make two 100× saccharide stocks (F and G) as described in Table 2.

substeps.instruction: Stock F (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve xylose 468 mg L⁻¹, fucose 746 mg L⁻¹, ribose 2 567 mg L⁻¹, sucrose 6 613 mg L⁻¹, lactose 1 439 mg L⁻¹, fructose 511 mg L⁻¹, arabinose 1 862 mg L⁻¹, trehalose 22 902 mg L⁻¹, gentiobiose 8 432 mg L⁻¹, D+ galactose 90 000 mg L⁻¹, sodium pyruvate 55 000 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.
Stock G (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve glucose 292 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.

steps.title: Prepare vitamin stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make two 100× vitamin stocks (H and I) according to Table 2.

substeps.instruction: Stock H (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve i‑inositol 200 mg L⁻¹, niacinamide 100 mg L⁻¹, choline chloride 100 mg L⁻¹, d‑calcium pantothenate 100 mg L⁻¹, thiamine monophosphate 100 mg L⁻¹, pyridoxine hydrochloride 100 mg L⁻¹, riboflavin‑5′‑phosphate Na 10 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.
Stock I (alkali‑soluble, 100×): dissolve folic acid 100 mg L⁻¹ in 1 M NaOH, then dilute with sterile water to 100×.

steps.title: Prepare inorganic salt stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make two inorganic‑salt stocks (J and K) and add NaHCO₃ separately just before SGM preparation.

substeps.instruction: Stock J (water‑soluble, 100×): dissolve MgSO₄ 49.8 mg L⁻¹, KH₂PO₄ 46 mg L⁻¹, Na₂HPO₄·12H₂O 190 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.
Stock K (water‑soluble, 25×): dissolve NaCl 2 000 mg L⁻¹, KCl 10 mg L⁻¹, MgCl₂ 2.3 mg L⁻¹, CaCl₂ 3.5 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.
Add NaHCO₃ as a solid (100 mg per 100 mL final SGM) just before mixing the medium.

steps.title: Prepare phenol red stock solution
steps.instruction: Make a 100× phenol‑red solution (L) by dissolving phenol red 1 mg L⁻¹ in sterile water.

steps.title: Store all stock solutions
steps.instruction: Aliquot each stock solution (A–L) into sterile containers and store at –80 °C until needed.

steps.title: Prepare shrimp ovary and eye‑stalk extracts
steps.instruction: Aseptically dissect shrimp ovary or eye‑stalk tissue, homogenize, incubate, and filter‑sterilize as described.

substeps.instruction: Weigh tissue, add sterile water at 20 mL g⁻¹, keep on ice and homogenize.
Incubate homogenate in a 60 °C water bath for 1 h with intermittent shaking.
Freeze the homogenate once, then thaw completely.
Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 2 h at 4 °C.
Collect supernatant, filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm vacuum filter, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare gelatin aqueous solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve gelatin powder in water at 60 °C, then cool to 37 °C before use.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 8.6 g gelatin (8.6 % m/v) per 100 mL final medium.
Add gelatin to water and heat to 60 °C until fully dissolved.
Cool the solution to 37 °C; keep it liquid until mixed with other components.

steps.title: Prepare optimal shrimp cell growth medium (SGM)
steps.instruction: Combine gelatin solution, diluted stock solutions, supplements, and adjust pH and osmolarity to obtain 100 mL of SGM.

substeps.instruction: In a sterile container, place 46 mL of the 8.6 % gelatin solution (contains 8.6 g gelatin) and keep at 37 °C.

Add each 100× stock solution (A–L) to the gelatin solution in the order listed in Table 2, using the volume percentages shown in Fig. 3 (e.g., 0.5 mL of stock A, 0.2 mL of stock B, etc.). Mix immediately after each addition.
Add solid NaHCO₃ (100 mg).
Measure pH; adjust to 7.2 ± 0.2 with 1 M HCl or 1 M NaOH as needed.
Measure osmolarity; adjust to 620 ± 20 mOsm·kg⁻¹ by adding sterile NaCl solution.
Bring the final volume to 100 mL with sterile water.
Filter‑sterilize the complete medium through a 0.22 µm filter.

Just before use, add growth factors and antibiotics: 20 µg L⁻¹ epidermal growth factor (EGF), 20 µg L⁻¹ basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF), 1 × 10⁵ IU L⁻¹ penicillin G sodium, 1 × 10⁵ IU L⁻¹ streptomycin, and 0.25 mg L⁻¹ amphotericin B.
Store the finished SGM at 4 °C; use within one month.

steps.title: Warm SGM before use
steps.instruction: Melt the gelatinous SGM by incubating at 37 °C for ~15 min (for 100 mL) before adding cells.

steps.title: Isolate shrimp hemocytes
steps.instruction: Collect hemolymph from anesthetized shrimp and purify hemocytes using anticoagulant and PBS washes.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize shrimp by immersion in 75 % ethanol for ~10 s.
Disinfect the sampling area sequentially with 75 % alcohol then iodophor; dry with sterile paper.
Using a 2.5‑mL syringe pre‑loaded with 0.5 mL anticoagulant solution (Table 3), draw hemolymph from the ventral sinus.
Centrifuge the hemolymph at 1 000 × g for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2× PBS containing a 30× antibiotic mixture; incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge again at 1 000 × g for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash the pellet once with 2× PBS (centrifuge as above).

steps.title: Culture hemocytes in SGM
steps.instruction: Resuspend washed hemocytes in optimal SGM, seed plates, and maintain culture.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the final cell pellet in pre‑warmed SGM (37 °C).
Seed cells into appropriate culture plates (e.g., 96‑well, 24‑well, etc.).
Incubate at 28 °C with 3 % CO₂.
Replace half of the medium every 2–3 days with fresh pre‑warmed SGM.

steps.title: Calcein‑AM viability staining
steps.instruction: Stain cultured hemocytes with 1 µM Calcein‑AM to assess live‑cell percentage.

substeps.instruction: Dilute Calcein‑AM stock in serum‑free medium to a working concentration of 1 µM.
Remove old medium from each well and wash cells 1–2 times with 2× PBS.
Add the Calcein‑AM working solution (100 µL per well of a 96‑well plate, 250 µL for 24‑well, 500 µL for 12‑well, 1 mL for 6‑well).
Gently shake the plate to cover all cells and incubate 45 min at 28 °C in darkness.
Wash cells once with 2× PBS, add fresh medium, and observe green fluorescence under an inverted fluorescence microscope.

steps.title: EdU proliferation assay
steps.instruction: Detect DNA synthesis in hemocytes using the BeyoClick™ EdU kit and subsequent click chemistry.

substeps.instruction: Prepare EdU working solution (1× EdU, 10 µM) by diluting the kit stock in SGM; add to wells containing seeded cells and incubate 24 h at 28 °C.
Remove medium and add 1 mL of 3.7 % formaldehyde in PBS; fix 15 min at room temperature.
Wash cells 3 times with 1 mL washing solution (3 % BSA in PBS, pH 7.4) for 3–5 min each.
Add 1 mL permeabilization reagent (0.3 % Triton X‑100 in PBS) and incubate 10–15 min at room temperature.
Wash 1–2 times with washing solution (3 % BSA in PBS) for 3–5 min each.
Prepare fresh click‑reaction mixture (use within 15 min): 430 µL click‑reaction buffer, 20 µL CuSO₄ solution, 1 µL azide‑488, 50 µL click additive; mix gently.
Add 0.5 mL click‑reaction solution to each well, gently shake to cover cells, and incubate 30 min at room temperature in darkness.
Wash cells 3 times with washing solution (3 % BSA in PBS) for 3–5 min each.
Prepare 1× Hoechst 33342 by diluting the 1000× stock 1:1000 in PBS.
Add 1 mL 1× Hoechst 33342 to each well, incubate 15 min at room temperature in darkness.
Wash cells 3 times with washing solution (3 % BSA in PBS) for 3–5 min each.
Proceed to fluorescence imaging to quantify EdU‑positive (proliferating) cells.

description: The optimization of shrimp cell growth medium (SGM) was based on both the composition of l-15 medium and the nutrient composition and content of shrimp serum (free amino acids, free saccharides and free fatty acids, etc.). In detail, on the basis of l-15 medium components, the SGM medium was optimized by removing all the components of amino acids from l-15 medium and then sequentially adding varied folds of the shrimp serum-based amino acid mixtures, or shrimp serum-based saccharide mixtures, or shrimp serum-based fatty acid mixture and other organic and inorganic supplements such as FBS, gelatin, and so on, which listed in Table 1. A total of 16 kinds of shrimp cell basic media (SBM) and 16 kinds of SGMs had been prepared and tested to obtain the formulation of the optimal SGM. The detailed optimization process and evaluation of these media can be found in related paper titled by routine development of long-term primary cell culture and finite cell line from the hemolymph of greasyback shrimp (Metapenaeus ensis) and virus susceptibility [1].
